messages:
marco: Heads-up — saw a weird pattern this morning where per-AZ batch sizes diverged during a regional spillback. Not the usual headroom creep, more like one AZ was batching 2x larger on average for ~10m and the autoscaler undershot.
anya: ugh that rings a bell. Did you correlate with network egress / pod restarts?
marco: quick check: no restarts, but we had transient inter-AZ latency spikes (p50->p95 jump) in the same window. My hypothesis: backlog routing moved requests into fewer GPUs in that AZ, causing queue depth to spike and batch aggregator to pack bigger batches, which then pushed GPU memory and slowed throughput.
wei: interesting — that could change our batch distribution metrics and trick the autoscaler which expects stable per-GPU throughput. Do you have a query?
marco: throwing this up as a proposal: add a Grafana panel and alert that looks at per-az batch-size percentiles + a heatmap of batch-size vs queue_slope. Draft PromQL for the heatmap: ```
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(redwood_inference_batch_size_bucket[1m])) by (le, az))
```
but we should actually produce a matrix of quantiles per az: ```
sum by (az, le) (rate(redwood_inference_batch_size_bucket[5m]))
```
cassie: can we instead compute percents per AZ then compare to cluster median? e.g. per_az_p95 / global_p95 > 1.4 triggers a warning. Also tie it to autoscaler decisions: if variance high + queue_slope positive then hold scale-down.
anya: love the "hold scale-down" rule. We've seen oscillation when one AZ inflates batch sizes and the autoscaler scales up another AZ, then they rebalance. proposal: synthetic probe that emits small constant requests to each AZ to measure steady-state batching behavior. label them synthetic_probe=true.
wei: synthetic probes are good but cost/quotas matter. Maybe run at 1 rps per AZ, sample 1% of traffic flagged, and a separate metric redwood_inference_synth_batch_size{probe="true"}. That avoids noise from real traffic.
marco: agreed. Panel list I propose: 1) per-AZ p50/p95 batch size time series, 2) batch-size vs queue_slope heatmap (5m window), 3) synth-probe latency + batch-size, 4) per-AZ autoscaler-decisions overlay (scale events as annotations).
cassie: add cost flag — if autoscaler holds scale-down for >10m due to variance we should emit an ops.note for capacity-cost review. Might need a burner alert for finance.
anya: for alerts: two phases. Warning: per-az_p95 / global_p95 > 1.3 for 10m AND queue_slope_avg > 0.1 for 5m. Sev: ratio > 1.5 AND queue_slope_avg > 0.2 AND synth_probe_batch_p95 > baseline+30%.
marco: here's a sample PromQL for the ratio: ```
(quantile_over_time(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (az, le)[10m:1m])
) / (quantile_over_time(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le)[10m:1m]))
```
I know that's messy — needs refinement.
wei: I'll convert to proper recording rules. Also we should tag metrics with node_gpu_model & pool so we can rule out if it's only older GPUs.
cassie: operational playbook note: if alert fires, first check synth_probe metrics, then the az routing table (traffic-engineering), then GPUs in that AZ for mem pressure. Don't blindly add capacity.
anya: can someone draft the grafana panel JSON snippets? I can wire the alert rules once we have recording rules.
marco: I'll prototype the heatmap and synthetic probe changes in a branch today. tagging @alerts-bot to kick off a test: please mute noise if we generate test alerts. :pray:
alerts-bot: created temporary silence for alerts from #eng-infra for 30m to allow testing.
wei: perfect — I'll follow up with recording rule PR and a short runbook doc. thanks all. :thumbsup:
